To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the dynamics of the efficient allocation are locally well-behaved, (ii) there are no oscillations in the dynamics of the one-sector neoclasical model and (iii) oscillations can result in the two-sector model only if the consumption sector is sufficiently capital-intensive.

(1) in economies with production, the local dynamics of efficient intertemporal allocations are well defined and (2) the dynamics of efficient inter-temporal allocations are locally stable, with the exception of a special case where the economy is sufficiently close to being a pure consumption economy.
the local dynamics of efficient intertemporal allocations are well behaved in the sense that they converge to a steady state and that this result holds under very general assumptions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the local dynamics of efficient intertemporal allocations in economies with many agents, production and recursive preferences.
a class of economies where the agents are characterized by heterogeneous preferences and production possibilities.
the local dynamics of efficient intertemporal allocations in economies where there are many agents and the technology is recursive.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in economies with many agents and production, the local dynamics of efficient intertemporal allocations are similar to those of economies with one agent and no production, provided that the utility functions satisfy the normality and increasing-marginal-impatience conditions, and that the consumption sector is not too capital intensive.

the dynamics of efficient allocations in economies with many agents, production and recursive preferences are locally stable, and that the presence of production and/or the absence of time separability are necessary conditions to obtain oscillations in the dynamics of efficient intertemporal allocations.
, in the absence of capital market imperfections, the local dynamics of efficient intertemporal allocations are not very sensitive to the degree of heterogeneity in preferences and technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the local dynamics of the efficient allocations are similar to those of a representative-agent economy with recursive preferences, provided that every individual agent's preferences satisfy the normality and increasing impatience conditions.

the dynamics of efficient allocations with recursive preferences and production are similar to the ones obtained with standard time-separable utility, except that the latter may lead to more complex dynamics in the case of a two-sector technology.

in economies with many heterogeneous agents, recursive but not time separable preferences, and production, there exists a unique steady state which can be reached by the dynamics, provided that every individual's utility is sufficiently well-behaved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the presence of a large number of agents, the dynamics of the economy are well behaved, even when the agents' preferences are recursive.
